Astraea mounts vnto the Throne. Mount Emperesse, whose praise for Peace shall mount, Whose glory, which thy solid vertues wonne, Shall honour Europe whil'st there shines a Sunne. Crown'd with Heauens inward beauties, worlds applause, Thron'd and reposd within the louing feare Of thy adoring Subiects: liue as long As Time hath life, and Fame a worthy tongue. Still breath our glory, the worlds Empresse, Religions Gardian, Peaces patronesse; Now flourish Arts, the Queene of Peace doth raigne, Vertue triumph, now shee doth sway the stemme, Who giues to Vertue, honours Diadem. All sing Paeans to her sacred worth, Which none but Angels tongues can warble forth: Yet sing, for though we cannot light the Sunne, Yet vtmost might hath kinde acceptance wonne.
